scope: Proposition 2.9 (Known-solution envelopes) of the manuscript “The Boltzmann–Grad limit for stable radial potentials on regular kinetic intervals” (preprints/The-Boltzmann-Grad-limit-for-stable-radial-potentials-on-regular-kinetic-intervals-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 364 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dce9fe5976f17b89), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 12-13. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose f is the classical nonnegative solution in the statement, and A = sup 0≤t≤T ∥f(t)∥∞,2β < ∞, B0 = ∥f0∥Bol,2β + ∥∇xf0∥Bol,2β < ∞. 12 Then sup 0≤t≤T (∥f(t)∥Bol,β + ∥∇xf(t)∥Bol,β) ≤ C(A, B0, β, T) < ∞. (2.23) Fix, once and for all, β0 = β/2. (2.24) Thus all independent inputs f(t) and their spatial Lipschitz envelopes have a common bound with the fixed margin β − β0. Constants in (2.23) are independent of the subsequent time-layer subdivision.
